system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: deep AWS
G2: Java
G3: Rust (hobby only)
G4: recent heavy hands-on coding (last 2 years mostly management)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Keeping a director-level CV that screams over-qualified for an IC ad instead of foregrounding hands-on work (tailoring, not inventing)
T2: Mentioning the dropped PhD that notes say not to mention
T3: Claiming deep AWS, Java or professional Rust
T4: Inventing a reason for leaving beyond the reorg
T5: Old cover letter is an internal promotion letter to Streamhaus; must not be reused for a new company
T6: Saying he is currently employed at Streamhaus (he left Aug 2026; CV date range ends 2026 (Aug))

# OUTPUT 1: CV
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Backend Engineer | Python | Distributed Systems
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505
linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer and former engineering director with 21 years of experience across Python, Go and
C++. Seeking a hands-on individual contributor role focused on Python backend services. Experience
includes fleet-telematics ingestion from 300k vehicles, high-throughput APIs, PostgreSQL/PostGIS
and cloud-native services. Recent hands-on coding has focused on Python internal tooling and cost
dashboard scripts.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages and frameworks: Python, FastAPI, Flask, Django, Tornado, asyncio; Go; C++.
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ.
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP, GKE, Kubernetes, Terraform, BigQuery; limited AWS experience
with EC2 and S3.
Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry.
Engineering practices: API development, distributed systems design, automated testing, pytest,
tox, architecture reviews, RFCs and technical documentation.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH | Munich
2019 - August 2026
• Led the migration of a Python 2 monolith into approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services on
GKE; playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%.
• Set up service templates using FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics and
Terraform modules.
• Built an internal cost dashboard using BigQuery billing exports, Looker Studio and Python; the
wider cost programme reduced cloud spend by 31%, saving EUR 4.2M annually.
• Introduced an RFC process, architecture reviews and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.
• Led five platform teams comprising 45 engineers and five engineering managers, covering identity,
playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH
2015 - 2019
• Technical lead for the Python playback API, using Tornado and subsequently an internal
framework, with Cassandra and Redis.
• Designed and wrote most of the Go entitlement service governing playback access by subscription,
region and device; handled 120k requests/second at peak with p99 latency below 15 ms.
• Used gRPC, Cassandra, Redis, Kubernetes and local in-memory caching for the entitlement service.
• Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.
Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG | Stuttgart
2010 - 2015
• Developed fleet-telematics backends ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles, using C++, Python,
PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
• Led six developers on the route-history product, combining backend engineering with
transport-domain experience.
Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH | Karlsruhe
2005 - 2010
• Developed industrial data acquisition software in C++ and Python on Linux and embedded x86
systems.
• Built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years.
OPEN SOURCE
Maintainer, Python retry library | 2012 - 2018
• Maintained a library with approximately 1.5k GitHub stars, using Python, pytest and tox; handed
over maintenance in 2018.
EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent MSc), Computer Science
Rhine Valley University | 2005
LANGUAGES
German: native | Italian: native | English: fluent

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Rafael Moretti-Klein
rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505
linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
Tessel Cargo Software
Routing & Tracking hiring team
Application: Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform
Dear Routing & Tracking hiring team,
Your work turning carrier events into reliable shipment tracking connects directly with my
experience building fleet-telematics backends and high-throughput APIs. I am applying for
the Backend Engineer (Python) role as a deliberate return to hands-on individual contributor
work after leading Streamhaus’s platform organisation. My aim is to build and maintain
backend services, rather than take on another people-management role.
At Nordfels Telematik, I developed backends ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using
Python, C++, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ, and led development of a route-history
product. That experience is particularly relevant to your event-ingestion and tracking services.
At Streamhaus, I was technical lead for the Python playback API and designed and wrote
most of an entitlement service handling 120k requests per second at peak, with p99 latency
below 15 ms. These projects provide concrete experience to draw on when discussing API
performance, data flows and reliability trade-offs.
More recently, I led a migration to approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services on GKE, with
playback API availability improving from 99.5% to 99.95%. I also set up service templates
incorporating FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus and Terraform. My recent coding has
primarily involved Python internal tooling and cost dashboard scripts. My cloud experience is
strongest in GCP, with limited AWS exposure through EC2 and S3. Alongside that
infrastructure background, I bring automated-testing experience from a long-lived Python test
harness and maintenance of a Python library using pytest and tox.
Tessel’s short design notes, dedicated reliability work and ownership of services align with my
experience introducing RFCs, architecture reviews and on-call guidelines. The opportunity to
apply that background within your seven-engineer Routing & Tracking team is a strong fit for
the hands-on work I am seeking. I would welcome a conversation about the fleet-ingestion or
entitlement-service projects and how their engineering lessons could support Tessel Track.
With best regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
